causal_retelling: Researchers tested an AI harvest rule against predefined rules in simulations, so they could examine possible catch and breeding-stock tradeoffs. One simulated case left more breeding biomass with large annual catch swings; another caught more while leaving less breeding biomass than its own comparison. But those results do not establish a management advantage, which means candidate rules should be tested against common catch-pattern and breeding-stock goals before claiming a real-world winner.

single_question_answered: What makes an AI fishing rule worth further testing? It supplies simulated alternatives whose catch and breeding-stock tradeoffs still need evaluation against shared management goals.
ending_assessment: The closing question follows from the tradeoffs and shared-goals recommendation. It invites a choice about management priorities rather than pretending the simulations determine the right balance.
candid_notes: The phrase simulated gains briefly compresses mixed outcomes into a positive label, but the immediate caveat prevents a claim of overall superiority.
The biology-change question is answered qualitatively through two separate cases; the narration appropriately says each has its own comparison.
